newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian finance stocks weak on central bank move.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian finance stocks weak on central bank move.

text.p: Shares of several Malaysian finance-based companies fell on Thursday morning amid worries over the effects of Bank Negara's curbs on property and share financing, analysts said.
Sime Darby Bhd, TA Enterprise Bhd, Affin Holdings Bhd and MBf Capital Bhd were among the most actively traded stocks in the morning session, falling between six and 55 cents each.
"Sime Darby is being transformed into a financial conglomerate, with Sime Bank contributing substantially to the group," said Victor Wan.

On Friday, the central bank announced plans to restrict banks and finance companies from lending more than 20 percent of their total outstanding loans for property purchases, and to maintain the restrictions on lending for share purchasing.

The restrictions had induced stockbroking companies to reduce their margin financing for share purchases, dealers said, causing punters who could not meet the new cash requirements to sell their stock, adding to the negative sentiment.

"Everyone will be doing forced selling today, not just TA," said a TA Securities dealer. "I think all margin, credit facilities have been withdrawn or partially withdrawn" following the Bank Negara ruling, he said.
MBf Capital was also sold down as the company has significant lending exposure to property development, analysts said.
"MBf Capital has a lot of lending in intercompany loans for the group's property projects. It is very big on property financing and also on retail share financing," said Wan.
